Reasoned review: Beacon, Paketo CPython, and Project Installer
2026-10-26

Final counts and classifier comparison (H/S = hostile/suspicious):
  s2_beacon.dll:       5/5 -> 4/5; ML flagged -> flagged (0.995 -> 0.995).
  Paketo module ZIP:   0/0 -> 0/0; ML benign -> benign (0.81535 -> 0.81535).
  ProjectInstaller:   3/3 -> 3/3; ML flagged -> benign (0.950 -> 0.89303).
  Archive-member H/S are all zero both times. The sole removed original
  finding is the false dnsstager identity on alphabetic padding. No supported
  attack capability was lost. The installer's classifier disagreement and
  nested-stage detection limitation remain and are detailed below.

Verdicts

s2_beacon.dll: MALICIOUS. Native x86 Cobalt Strike 3.x-style reflective DNS
Beacon with a populated operator configuration, token theft/impersonation,
process launch, and injection capabilities. Cobalt Strike can be used in an
authorized assessment; no deployment authorization is supplied. The configured
remote-control implant and credential-token abuse tip the on-machine judgment.

python-runtime Go module ZIP: BENIGN. CPython Cloud Native Buildpack source,
version v1.18.45-0.20260918145118-59d378082acb. forager recovered the exact
version from proxy.golang.org, verified its Go checksum-database record, and
produced the same archive SHA-256 as the supplied artifact. This corroborates
integrity, rather than making the source automatically trustworthy. The read
runtime/build/CI paths explain its capabilities without a theft or backdoor
chain. External action versions and subsequently downloaded dependencies are
outside the supplied bytes; this is not an attestation of every future fetch.

ProjectInstaller.exe: MALICIOUS. A Node 22.23.1/pkg executable whose V8 caches
hide an embedded native payload. The administrator-gated path attempts broad
Defender exclusions, XOR-decodes the embedded PE, writes a random ProgramData
EXE and launches it hidden/detached. Its decoded native stage also contains a
local AMSI patch. These effects tip the judgment independently of the filename,
package's self-description, model score, or successful execution on a victim.
No deployment authorization or original distribution context is assumed.

Independent reverse engineering

Beacon:
  Parsed PE sections, imports, exports and entry point. Exported
  _ReflectiveLoader@4 at VA 0x10008c79 walks PEB/module/export structures,
  uses ROR13 name hashing, allocates/copies an image and resolves its imports.
  The native DLL contains the actual DNS, token and injection implementations.
  XOR-0x69 decoding at file offset 0x2f228 yields typed BE setting records:
    DNS mode 1; port 443; sleep 5000 ms; jitter 0; maximum data 1048576;
    ns7.softline.top, ns8.softline.top, ns9.softline.top;
    Amazon-shaped request paths and Host: www.amazon.com profile strings;
    rundll32 spawn paths in syswow64/sysnative; msagent pipe template.
  This is a populated operator configuration, not just a product-name string.
  Rizin traces fcn.10009ce8 taking a PID, OpenProcess -> OpenProcessToken ->
  ImpersonateLoggedOnUser -> DuplicateTokenEx, retaining the primary token at
  0x1003c6b4. fcn.10003786 consumes that token in CreateProcessAsUserA with a
  CreateProcessWithTokenW fallback. fcn.10005721 allocates remote memory,
  writes the supplied buffer and changes its protection. fcn.100062e1 reads
  a suspended thread's integer context, changes its start register and calls
  SetThreadContext/ResumeThread. No process-image replacement was inferred.
  DNS helpers at 0x1000357b/0x1000361b request TXT/AAAA records and copy returned
  data; the surrounding code constructs the Beacon label templates.
  The 138647-byte overlay is predominantly alphabetic padding, not another PE.
  The third-party dnsstager finding pairs resolver code at 197259 with ASCII
  hdnsa at 243879 inside that padding. The latter is not an executed push-dnsa
  instruction and does not establish the named dnsstager resource.

Paketo:
  Read detect/build/installer/pip cleanup and launch environment code, the
  tool-download helpers, compilation/test scripts and CI workflows.
  run/main.go binds ordinary configure/make/python3 executables into packit.
  Detect derives requirements from BP_CPYTHON_VERSION/configure flags. Build
  resolves a manifest dependency, reuses a checksum-matched layer, otherwise
  delivers a binary or compiles configure -> make -> make altinstall, generates
  an SBOM, sets Python environment paths and makes interpreter symlinks.
  Optional cleanup uninstalls setuptools in the contributed layer. exec.d
  emits TOML environment configuration, not a hidden launch mechanism.
  tools.sh downloads named build tools from their upstream GitHub releases,
  marks them executable and invokes them as packaging/test tooling. Release
  workflows publish buildpack assets/images, upload dependency metadata and
  create maintenance PRs. Secrets feed those authenticated operations.
  pull_request_target labels PRs; it is not evidence of a supplied attack.
  The AWS action in update-dependencies-from-metadata.yml explicitly supplies
  stored access-key inputs. Action presence alone does not prove OIDC.
  No hostile or suspicious findings fired in any archive member. Neutral
  network, execution, permissions and credential-reference observations remain.

Installer:
  PE entry and TLS callbacks belong to the real Node runtime, not a RET-only
  decoy. Recovered the pkg VFS manifest and original serialized V8 modules:
    payload offset 57440768;
    index cache [0,5040], payload cache [5535,1026808], UI shell [1032466,4968].
  Retrieved the exact upstream Node v22.23.1 V8 bytecodes.h with forager.
  Used its opcode definitions to decode the cached routines without invoking
  JavaScript or launching the specimen. The main routine tests administrator
  status through execSync('net session') and either exits with a prompt or
  enters saveAndRun. The latter invokes the exclusion routine and decryptor,
  constructs a ProgramData random EXE path, calls writeFileSync with the
  decoded bytes, then spawn with that same path, empty argv and hidden/ignored
  stdio/detach options. It unrefs the child and exits.
  The Base64 command decodes to hidden PowerShell Add-MpPreference exclusions
  for TEMP, ProgramData and two Windows/Microsoft subtrees, then gpupdate.
  Decoder bytecode at cache offsets 0xc80..0xcef takes Buffer.from(base64),
  allocates an output buffer and stores input[i] XOR key.charCodeAt(i%length).
  The write and later launcher share the same pathname register at offsets
  0xf1d/0xf5d/0xf60. Constant-pool and context bindings were followed manually;
  two generic call opcodes do not provide those names to the rule matcher.
  Base64/XOR extraction recovers a 769536-byte PE, SHA-256:
    73c4bf3abc84e6826efb1690ae6c2a255af5465dd369f9323e48283219076e35
  Its string helpers rotate each byte right by i%7+1, then XOR with
  (13*i+177)&255. Traced that arithmetic in disassembly and decoded 210
  referenced strings, including AmsiOpenSession, CoGetObject, boot-task and
  RuntimeBroker path references. These strings alone do not prove every action.
  To verify the AMSI path, isolated Unicorn instruction emulation at
  0x140069290 intercepted every out-of-routine call. It resolved AmsiOpenSession,
  passed its address to VirtualProtect and wrote the actual 48 31 c0 patch
  buffer via current-process WriteProcessMemory. This validates the static
  target/buffer relationship, not successful Windows API execution. No specimen
  ran on the host; no sandbox-only operation was added to the rules.

Rule corrections and preservation

1. Moved the AWS action reference from CI permission to CI step, removing the
   unsupported OIDC claim. Preserved matcher, criticality, platform/file scope
   and both existing objective exclusions. No permission/step directory-wide
   consumers depended on the moved member; broader CI membership is unchanged.
2. Moved UTF-16 include/require call text to source syntax/call/invocation.
   Embedded Node source actually matched the former PHP-labeled atom.
   Preserved its matcher and notable severity; updated the PHP composite,
   which independently still requires PHP-tag context. Audited ancestor refs.
3. Moved the former V8 dropper composite to XOR concealment and named it for
   the supported profile. Generic XOR plus shared-argument calls proves
   neither callee identity, a downloaded/dropped executable, nor C2. Retained
   every original bytecode/path condition and both exclusions, and required
   the independent hidden Defender-exclusion objective for hostile admission.
   The known malicious installer still matches. The hosts-sinkhole consumer
   retains the moved alternative. The Python-only staging consumer could not
   select this PE-only rule. The encoding ancestor's stego consumer admits the
   concealment observation; the new rule supplies neither of its required
   stego-marker legs.
4. Changed the existing overlay spawn-name observation to raw byte matching.
   The 200000-string budget dropped this short serialized token from the
   binary text corpus. Its word boundary and overlay restriction remain;
   it reports a name reference, not invocation or an executable payload.
5. Added an exact population property for dnsa-push candidate bytes: every
   candidate must lie after all mapped sections, within a 256+-letter run.
   Applied it only to the inaccurate GCTI dnsstager finding. A run may cross
   the overlay boundary, but every candidate must itself be in the overlay.
   Any additional real instruction candidate outside those runs leaves the
   original signature eligible. No filename, family identity or package
   exception is used. Native API hashing and DNS Beacon coverage is retained.

Controls and limitations

check.py copies controls outside testdata and checks AWS static-key/OIDC
references and unchanged consumer suppression, PHP and Node UTF-16 calls,
missing-call and spawn-word near misses, neutral generic V8 XOR/call evidence,
alphabetic-overlay and boundary-crossing false hits, and preserved executable
and mixed code/data DNS-signature matches. All control PEs are nonexecuted.
The baseline really flags the generic XOR/call control hostile and mislabels
the Node require syntax PHP. Those unsupported claims are corrected rather
than hidden by package exceptions or severity demotion.

Before editing shared rules, inspected their exact and ancestor consumers,
the existing V8 XOR/OR/missing-cache controls and historical native/Beacon
review records. Baseline/current scans of the existing hostile workflow
archive (gha-marrowworks-workflow-inject-linux.tgz), credential-pipeline benign
action, original V8 controls and recovered native PE retain every finding and
criticality. The recovered native PE retains five hostile/two suspicious
findings. The GCTI source's original positive hash was unavailable through
forager (MalwareBazaar, Triage, Malshare); no reconstructed file is represented
as that original. Retention tests use explicitly constructed real opcode
counterparts plus the existing corpus; external positive-corpus breadth is
limited. The entire upstream signature stays active outside the proven
alphabetic-overlay mismatch.

comparisons.json records matched input paths, counts and model probabilities,
including archive-member differences. Its only intended removed original
finding is the unsupported dnsstager resource identity. Other accurate traits
and severities are preserved under moves.json. No attack coverage is removed.
Both baseline and final comparisons use local slow scans with --follow=none.
The first preliminary scan used --follow none and reported an extra nonexistent
target named none; it is not the comparison baseline. A replay against a copy
of the original rules supplies the reproducible baseline.

The wrapper still has a detection gap: facts do not bind arbitrary serialized
V8 constant-pool/context callees, or automatically reconstruct its embedded
Base64 plus variable-key XOR PE. Thus the manually verified write-to-launch,
AMSI patch, persistence/elevation and remote-control stage cannot all become
independent hostile findings on the wrapper. Investigated a direct V8 payload
rule, but generic XOR, call-register reuse and API-name co-occurrence cannot
establish that full flow. Its neutral observations and intent-qualified XOR
profile remain. The wrapper has three hostile findings but fewer independent
hostile outcomes than that count suggests (two exclusion profiles overlap).
No additional quota-filling detections were invented. Standalone stage findings
are reported separately and are not counted as automatic wrapper coverage.

The model flags Beacon and agrees with the benign buildpack assessment.
After accurate profile/placement corrections it no longer flags the installer,
despite three hostile findings. This is a classifier miss, not a reason to
restore the generic dropper overclaim. The model reports feature schema v18
while the engine expects v21, a further limit on its interpretation of rules.

Evidence and provenance remain under:
  /usr/local/var/cyclotron/tmp.noindex/cyclotron-e78afdd4/scratch/review/
including original/final scans, cleave facts, rizin traces, carved caches,
decoded PE, isolated instruction trace, forager artifacts/provenance and logs.
Final acceptance command: make validate.

Marker lines (verbatim commit-body text):
  Cobalt Strike Beacon: C2 and token theft; fix padding signature
  Paketo CPython: verified buildpack; correct AWS OIDC claim
  Project Installer: exclusions and XOR stage; narrow V8 claim
